title: 2013 HMMT February Guts Problem 14
statement: Consider triangle \(A B C\) with \(\angle A=2 \angle B\). The angle bisectors from \(A\) and \(C\) intersect at \(D\), and the angle bisector from \(C\) intersects \(\overline{A B}\) at \(E\). If \(\frac{D E}{D C}=\frac{1}{3}\), compute \(\frac{A B}{A C}\).

solutions.text: \(\quad \frac{7}{9} \quad\) Let \(A E=x\) and \(B E=y\). Using angle-bisector theorem on \(\triangle A C E\) we have \(x: D E=A C: D C\), so \(A C=3 x\). Using some angle chasing, it is simple to see that \(\angle A D E=\angle A E D\), so \(A D=A E=x\). Then, note that \(\triangle C D A \sim \triangle C E B\), so \(y:(D C+D E)=x: D C\), so \(y: x=1+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{4}{3}\), so \(A B=x+\frac{4}{3} x=\frac{7}{3} x\). Thus the desired answer is \(A B: A C=\frac{7}{3} x: 3 x=\frac{7}{9}\).
